title: Cutroom — an AI-assisted video editor
brief: Upload footage, edit through a transcript, review AI suggestions and export an approved cut. A greenfield planning example with proposed pilot limits.
objective: An editor can turn an interview into a captioned clip without losing the original, and recover if upload, AI or rendering fails.
success: A user can upload, make a manual cut, accept or reject an AI suggestion, undo it, and export the selected revision.
A failed or repeated request cannot expose another workspace’s assets, duplicate an accepted edit or consume the same job budget twice.
Exported audio, video and captions agree with the reviewed timeline on the agreed reference-media fixtures.

now: Team workspaces, owner/editor/viewer roles, project library, resumable uploads and proxy previews.
Transcript corrections, single source-video track, cut/reorder, captions and simple audio gain.
AI transcript suggestions and reproducible server exports with progress, cancel and retry.
later: Multitrack editing, live collaboration, shared review links and automated billing.
More codecs, larger uploads, batch processing and additional language coverage after measurement.
out: AI-generated footage, voice cloning, autonomous publishing or a full desktop NLE replacement.

walkthroughs.title: Upload and prepare a video
walkthroughs.intro: Imagine you have an interview on your computer and want to start editing it.
walkthroughs.result: You get a private, playable preview. The original video remains unchanged.

steps.title: You choose a video
steps.explanation: The browser is the website you use. It asks the application to start an upload.

steps.title: The application checks your access
steps.explanation: It checks both who you are and whether this project belongs to a team you can edit. Signing in alone is not enough.

steps.title: Your file goes into private storage
steps.explanation: The application gives your browser temporary upload permission. The video goes into the private media bucket: storage for files.

steps.title: Preparation joins a waiting list
steps.explanation: The application adds a saved job to the queue. This lets the website respond while longer work waits its turn.

steps.title: A worker prepares a preview
steps.explanation: A worker is a background program. It takes the job, reads the video and saves a smaller version that is easier to play while editing.

steps.title: You see progress, then the preview
steps.explanation: The worker updates the database, which stores project records rather than the video itself. The website reads that saved status and shows the result.

walkthroughs.title: Get and review AI suggestions
walkthroughs.intro: You already have a project and want help finding useful cuts or removing pauses.
walkthroughs.result: You receive proposed edits. Nothing changes until you accept a proposal.

steps.title: You ask for editing help
steps.explanation: The website sends your request and the version of the edit you are looking at.

steps.title: The application checks access and budget
steps.explanation: The server checks project membership and processing limits before it queues the request.

steps.title: A worker asks the approved AI service
steps.explanation: The worker collects the approved audio or transcript spans. Only the selected material is sent for processing.

steps.title: The worker checks the returned suggestion
steps.explanation: AI output is treated as a proposal. Times must fit the real source video, and the proposal must refer to the current edit version.

steps.title: You inspect the proposed changes
steps.explanation: The website shows what would change. You can accept, reject or continue editing manually.

steps.title: Accepted changes become a new saved edit
steps.explanation: If you accept, the application saves a new edit version. It rejects an outdated proposal instead of overwriting newer work.

walkthroughs.title: Export the finished video
walkthroughs.intro: You have reviewed the timeline and want a downloadable video.
walkthroughs.result: You get a file made from the exact edit version you selected.

steps.title: You choose an edit version and export settings
steps.explanation: The website sends these choices to the application. Later edits will not silently change this export.

steps.title: The application records the export request
steps.explanation: It checks your permission and saves the chosen edit version and settings in the database.

steps.title: The export waits for a worker
steps.explanation: The queue keeps the request while a worker becomes available. You can leave the page and return to its saved status.

steps.title: The worker creates the finished video
steps.explanation: It reads the original files, applies the saved cuts and captions, and stores a new output file. It does not overwrite the original.

steps.title: The worker checks and records the result
steps.explanation: A successful output is attached to this job. Failed or cancelled jobs cannot publish a finished download.

steps.title: The website shows the result
steps.explanation: Saved progress tells your browser when the file is ready. Downloads still require access to the project.

walkthroughs.title: A successful export
walkthroughs.intro: Follow one export request from waiting to a finished file.
walkthroughs.result: The app publishes one checked output for this request.

steps.title: The request waits safely
steps.explanation: The queue records which edit version to render.

steps.title: A worker starts the job
steps.explanation: The worker reserves this attempt so another worker does not start the same attempt at the same time.

steps.title: The output is checked
steps.explanation: Finishing the render is not enough: the app checks that the expected video and audio output exists.

steps.title: The result becomes available
steps.explanation: Only a valid, uncancelled job is marked ready for download.

walkthroughs.title: Retry or cancel
walkthroughs.intro: A processing problem needs a clear next action, not an endless spinner.
walkthroughs.result: The job either retries within its limits or stops without publishing a late result.

steps.title: A failed attempt gets a reason
steps.explanation: A crashed worker or invalid output is recorded as a failure.

steps.title: A retry goes back to the queue
steps.explanation: The same logical request gets another bounded attempt. It should not charge or publish twice for one accepted result.

steps.title: Cancellation stops publication
steps.explanation: A waiting or running job can be cancelled. Even if its worker finishes late, that result must not become available.

sections.title: Data and API contracts that prevent lost edits

cells: Workspace / membership
User role and access boundary.
Membership is checked server-side; viewer cannot mutate.
Asset
Checksum, object key, duration, frame-rate/time-base and workspace.
Source object is immutable; untrusted format metadata is inspected.
Transcript revision
Timed text and human corrections.
Corrections never silently change the original media.
Edit revision
Ordered source ranges, caption choices and audio settings.
Milliseconds are validated against source bounds; server converts to media time bases.
AI proposal
Base revision, transcript revision, proposed operations.
Cannot apply if base revision changed or any span is invalid.
Render job
Immutable edit snapshot, attempt, usage, output and cancellation state.
A job cannot publish into a deleted project or another workspace.
POST /projects/:id/uploads
Media metadata + idempotency key → asset/upload session + signed parts.
403 membership; 413 configured size limit; 409 duplicate mismatch.
POST /uploads/:id/complete
Part checksums → processing asset; same completion can repeat safely.
Reject missing parts and mismatched owner; cleanup abandoned uploads.
PUT /projects/:id/edit
Expected revision + validated edit document → new revision.
409 stale revision returns enough state to recover; never overwrite silently.
POST /projects/:id/suggestions
Base edit + transcript revision + intent → job ID.
Insufficient budget, unsupported language or changed revision.
POST /projects/:id/exports
Revision + preset + idempotency key → render job ID.
Invalid range, unsupported profile or budget unavailable.
GET /jobs/:id and POST /jobs/:id/cancel
Persisted progress/result; cancel fences publication.
403 wrong workspace; reconnect reads status instead of assuming completion.

blocks.text: Workspace ID is derived from the authenticated project lookup, not trusted from the request body. Model output never supplies executable FFmpeg flags or arbitrary file URLs.

cells: Connection drops during upload
Resume remaining parts without a second asset.
Interrupt transfer and verify final checksum.
Speech provider is unavailable
Manual editing remains available; transcript job can retry.
Inject provider timeout and bounded retry.
AI proposes nonexistent time spans
Reject proposal with an understandable reason.
Validate every operation against source and transcript revisions.
Worker dies after output upload
Recover or clean up temporary output; show one finished export.
Kill worker between upload and commit.
Project deleted during rendering
Cancel/fence result and purge temporary objects.
Race deletion against completion and recheck storage.
User is removed from workspace
Existing page loses access on its next authorized request.
Revoke membership before signing/download/status requests.

items.detail: Queue age, worker failures, processing duration, output failures, provider errors and spend per workspace.

items.label: Recovery
items.detail: Restore metadata and verify links to object inventory in an isolated environment. Never claim metadata backup alone restores deleted media.
